source: Pan, Xie, Wilson (2025) Large Language Models Think Too Fast To Explore Effectively
finding: Five LLMs played Little Alchemy 2 (720 elements, 500 trials). Only o1 and DeepSeek-R1 beat the human average. The other models were below humans.
numbers: Elements found in 500 trials: LLaMA3.1-8B 9, LLaMA3.1-70B 25, GPT-4o 35, human 42, DeepSeek-R1 85, o1 177. Human benchmark 29,493 players, 4,691,033 trials. o1 t=9.71, GPT-4o t=-5.48. Five runs per temperature.
limits: Preprint under review. One game. Human mean 51 across all trials.
agent_relevance: Open-ended probe choice is a weak spot of plain models. A reasoning-trained model changed the result more than any prompt did.

source: Pan, Xie, Wilson (2025) Large Language Models Think Too Fast To Explore Effectively
finding: Regression of choices on empowerment (future-combination potential) and uncertainty (rarely used elements). Most LLMs have near-zero empowerment weight, far below humans. o1 is above humans.
numbers: Higher temperature raised the uncertainty weight (beta=2.911, z=7.44, p<0.001) but not empowerment (beta=0.196, z=1.067, p=0.286). Temperature gave a small score gain (beta=0.124, z=5.06).
limits: Empowerment values come from a neural network fitted to human data (Brandle et al.), not a true mutual-information estimate.
agent_relevance: Sampling noise adds novelty seeking only. A probe score based on reach or control must be computed explicitly, in code.

source: Pan, Xie, Wilson (2025) Large Language Models Think Too Fast To Explore Effectively
finding: Sparse autoencoder probes on LLaMA3.1-70B: choice and uncertainty signals peak in the first layers, the empowerment signal peaks much later (layer 72). Authors say the model decides before empowerment is computed.
numbers: Choice weight peaks at layer 1 (beta=1.08). Uncertainty correlation peaks at layer 2. Empowerment correlation peaks at layer 72. Same pattern in the 8B model.
limits: Correlational. Picks the single most correlated SAE neuron. Ablating the empowerment neuron cut empowerment-guided behavior; ablating the uncertainty neuron caused collapse.
agent_relevance: Supports a separate, slow, explicit scoring step for probe choice instead of one-shot generation.

source: Pan, Xie, Wilson (2025) Large Language Models Think Too Fast To Explore Effectively
finding: Mitigations did not fix standard LLMs. Prompt engineering and feature steering gave no significant gain. R1 reasoned longer and with more varied reasoning types than GPT-4o with chain of thought.
numbers: Appendix C: no significant improvement from prompt tuning or intervention. R1 and GPT-4o traces were labelled into 7 categories by GPT-4.1 (first 150 trials).
limits: Labels from an LLM classifier. R1 and GPT-4o differ in training, not only in token count.
agent_relevance: Prompting alone is a weak lever for exploration. Spending test-time compute on listing options and past trials is what worked.

source: Lidayan, Du, Kosoy, Rufova, Abbeel, Gopnik (2025) Intrinsically-Motivated Humans and Agents in Open-World Exploration
finding: Humans and RL agents played Crafter with no goal. Human exploration progress correlated positively with Entropy and Empowerment. Information Gain did not correlate consistently.
numbers: Up to 20 minutes of play. 51 children (6-12 years) and 24 adults recruited. 13 agents per setting trained for 1M steps, plus a random agent. Private speech: 17 children and 23 adults gave transcripts.
limits: Small human samples. Authors explain Information Gain can be high from trying many actions that do nothing.
agent_relevance: Information gain alone is a weak probe score. Pair it with a measure of effect or control so probes that change the world count.

source: Lidayan, Du, Kosoy, Rufova, Abbeel, Gopnik (2025) Intrinsically-Motivated Humans and Agents in Open-World Exploration
finding: Across humans and agents, Entropy rises fast early then plateaus, while Empowerment keeps rising. Authors suggest state diversity matters early and control later.
numbers: Humans keep higher Information Gain per episode than every agent. Intrinsic-reward agents (entropy, info gain, NovelD, APT) lost to an extrinsic-reward agent tailored to the game on most scores.
limits: Descriptive and correlational. One environment.
agent_relevance: Suggests a phase rule for S7: widen first, then favor probes that give control over outcomes.

source: Lidayan, Du, Kosoy, Rufova, Abbeel, Gopnik (2025) Intrinsically-Motivated Humans and Agents in Open-World Exploration
finding: Private speech in children: stating goals goes with better exploration.
numbers: Fraction of goal utterances vs mean achievement score in children: r=0.8, p=0.005. Children state goals in 21% of utterances, adults 10%. Breadth-depth correlation: children 0.51 (p=0.01), adults -0.27 (p=0.21).
limits: Preliminary. Few participants talked. An LLM did the utterance labelling.
agent_relevance: Stating the goal before choosing a probe may help. Cheap slot to test.

source: Massari, Biehl, Meeden, Kanai (2021) Experimental Evidence that Empowerment May Drive Exploration in Sparse-Reward Environments
finding: An empowerment-inspired reward (variational information bottleneck) helped an A2C agent in sparse grid worlds about as much as a VAE-based curiosity reward.
numbers: Four sparse-reward MiniGrid environments. Time-to-success compared with one-sided t-tests. One run was an outlier (cap 1e7 frames) and was removed in a second analysis. In DoorKey-8x8 the curious agent looked best.
limits: Few runs. Empowerment-inspired, not exact empowerment. Authors say more research is needed before it replaces information gain.
agent_relevance: Empowerment can stand in when explicit belief-update scoring is not available, but evidence is weak.

source: Massari, Biehl, Meeden, Kanai (2021) Experimental Evidence that Empowerment May Drive Exploration in Sparse-Reward Environments
finding: States the open theory question: empowerment maximization does not by itself imply information gain maximization, though good control may require a good model.
numbers: No new numbers for this point.
limits: Position inside an empirical paper.
agent_relevance: Keep the two as separate terms in any probe ranking.

source: Ellis, Myers, Tuyls, Levine, Dragan, Eysenbach (2025) Training LLM Agents to Empower Humans
finding: Fine-tuned an LLM assistant to maximize the human's empowerment using only offline text. Simulated human is Gemma-3-27B-it on 554 LiveCodeBench problems.
numbers: Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct trained with Empower more than doubles Pass@1 vs the strongest baseline. Abstract reports an average 192% gain in simulated human success over an SFT baseline.
limits: Competitive programming only. Simulated human is an LLM. Also tested with Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct as the human model (appendix).
agent_relevance: Shows empowerment works as an LLM objective, but it needs training. A scaffold cannot train.

source: Ellis, Myers, Tuyls, Levine, Dragan, Eysenbach (2025) Training LLM Agents to Empower Humans
finding: 18-person user study of a code-completion assistant. Empower preferred over a strong baseline.
numbers: 78% preferred it (p=0.015). Acceptance rate 8.08% vs 6.18% (p=0.0002). 208 vs 333 suggestions per user. 17 of 18 ranked it better on deletions. 26% fewer accepted characters deleted (p=0.012).
limits: N=18. Code only. Authors say real-world code may need a better estimator.
agent_relevance: Fewer, better-timed suggestions beat many. Fits the rule of acting only on a signal.

source: Bickford Smith, Kirchhof, Zhang, Rainforth (2026) BED-LLM: Intelligent Information Gathering with LLMs and Bayesian Experimental Design
finding: Pick the next question by expected information gain estimated from the LLM's own predictive distributions. Beats prompt-only questioning in 20 Questions across models.
numbers: Final success is typically more than double Prompt-Only. Qwen2.5-72B: Animals 100%, Celebrities 100%, Things 80%. GPT-4o: 100/100/80. Llama-3.3-70B: 90/70/70 (read from figure text).
limits: Answerer is an LLM, not a human. Exact string match. More LLM calls.
agent_relevance: Direct template for S7: propose candidate probes, estimate how well each splits the live hypotheses, choose in code.

source: Bickford Smith, Kirchhof, Zhang, Rainforth (2026) BED-LLM: Intelligent Information Gathering with LLMs and Bayesian Experimental Design
finding: Ablations: filtering hypotheses and estimating full EIG (not predictive entropy) both matter. Letting the LLM judge the most informative question still beats prompt-only and is cheap.
numbers: Entropy ablation was the strongest alternative, slightly above Split. Raw in-context belief updates were incoherent and overconfident, ignoring conversation history (Fig 7).
limits: Ranking read from tables and text. Not every cell captured.
agent_relevance: Keep the hypothesis list in code, not in the model's raw belief. Judged informativeness is a fallback.

source: Active Task Disambiguation with LLMs (ICLR 2025)
finding: Frames clarifying questions as Bayesian experimental design: pick the question that maximizes information gain over candidate solutions, not over questions. EIG strategies give higher code accuracy with fewer queries.
numbers: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4o-mini, Llama-3 8B and 70B on HumanEval and APPS, four requirement-eliciting iterations. Zero-shot GPT-4o-mini: 35% on APPS vs 70% on HumanEval.
limits: Gap between baseline and EIG shrinks for stronger models. Needs more LLM calls. A filtering step is needed against hallucinated requirements.
agent_relevance: Reason over the space of solutions, not only the space of questions.

source: Cooper, Wadhawan, Giorgi, Tan, Liang (2025) The Curious Language Model: Strategic Test-Time Information Acquisition
finding: CuriosiTree: greedy tree search over reasoning, retrieval, patient question and lab test, by expected information gain per cost. Beats random and self-evaluation action choice in simulated diagnosis.
numbers: Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct, tradeoff 0.1, 10 diagnoses x 50 trials per method (lupus in main text). Deliberation-only and retrieval-only never gave the correct lupus diagnosis. Of 95 reasoning steps, 84% kept the top diagnosis and in 62% of those entropy fell.
limits: Environment is an LLM oracle. Costs arbitrary. O(k*k*m) model calls.
agent_relevance: Cost-aware EIG fits S7 when probes have different prices (think, check, run).

source: Krishnamurthy, Harris, Foster, Zhang, Slivkins (2024) Can Large Language Models Explore In-Context?
finding: Of all configurations tried on bandits, only one explored well: GPT-4 with an explore hint, externally summarized history (per-arm averages) and chain of thought.
numbers: GPT-4 with the basic prompt suffers a suffix failure (never tries the best arm again) in over 60% of replicates. 48 configs for GPT-3.5 and Llama2, 72 for GPT-4. T=500 check with N=20.
limits: Simple multi-armed bandits. Summaries made outside the model.
agent_relevance: Summarize statistics in code before the model sees them. Raw history leads to premature lock-in.

source: Binz, Schulz (2023) Using cognitive psychology to understand GPT-3
finding: GPT-3 did well at described decisions and bandits but showed no signature of directed exploration in the horizon task, and failed causal reasoning.
numbers: Horizon task compared with human data. Short-horizon regret matched humans.
limits: GPT-3 only. Newer models not covered.
agent_relevance: Models do not by default prefer the more informative option. Information value has to be computed outside the model.
quote: it shows no signatures of directed exploration

source: Handa et al. (2024) Bayesian Preference Elicitation with Language Models (OPEN)
finding: OPEN: the LM proposes features, a Bayesian model picks questions by expected information gain. Accuracy over time beats LM-only questioning.
numbers: Metric is time-integrated delta accuracy, error bars one standard error. LM-only open-ended questions beat LM-only pairwise ones.
limits: Content recommendation domain. Specific numbers not extracted.
agent_relevance: Hybrid pattern: the model proposes, code computes information gain.

source: Gao et al. (2026) Navigate the Unknown: Enhancing LLM Reasoning with Intrinsic Motivation Guided Exploration (IMAGINE)
finding: Intrinsic exploration reward for RL training of reasoning LLMs (Qwen2.5 base). Improves PPO and GRPO on GSM8K, Countdown and AIME 2024.
numbers: AIME 2024: up to 22.23% relative improvement over GRPO (0.3667 accuracy). Training time rose, e.g. Countdown-34 GRPO 12.13h to 14.55h.
limits: Training method. Prediction-error style reward, not exact information gain.
agent_relevance: Shows intrinsic rewards help when training is allowed. Not usable in our scaffold.

source: LLM-Driven Intrinsic Motivation for Sparse Reward Reinforcement Learning (2025)
finding: Combining a VAE state-novelty reward with an LLM-derived reward helped an A2C agent in MiniGrid DoorKey where plain A2C failed to learn.
numbers: One environment. Plain A2C failed.
limits: Single small environment.
agent_relevance: The LLM can supply a goal-progress term while novelty supplies the exploration term.

source: Wen (2025) The Missing Reward: Active Inference in the Era of Experience
finding: Position paper: replace external reward with free-energy minimization, with an LLM as the generative world model.
numbers: No experiments.
limits: Proposal only.
agent_relevance: No measured benefit. Do not cite as evidence.

source: Prakki (2024) Active Inference for Self-Organizing Multi-LLM Systems
finding: An active-inference layer above an LLM agent chooses prompts and search actions. Reports a shift from information gathering to targeted prompt testing.
numbers: Three state factors, seven observation modalities. Qualitative. No benchmark score.
limits: Single author. No head-to-head baseline.
agent_relevance: Weak evidence. Shows an expected-free-energy loop inside an LLM agent.

source: Kulveit, von Stengel, Leventov (2023) Predictive Minds: LLMs As Atypical Active Inference Agents
finding: Argues LLMs fit the active-inference frame, except that they lack a tight loop between acting and perceiving the effect.
numbers: Conceptual. No data.
limits: Theory paper.
agent_relevance: An agent with probes and feedback closes that loop. That is the S7 loop.

source: Demircan et al. (2024) Sparse autoencoders reveal temporal difference learning in LLMs
finding: Cited by Pan et al. for the SAE method: LLMs form TD-like value representations in context. File downloaded but not read for results.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Not read.
agent_relevance: Background for SAE probing.

source: Brandle, Stocks, Tenenbaum, Gershman, Schulz (2023) Empowerment contributes to exploration behaviour in a creative video game
finding: Founding human study of empowerment in Little Alchemy 2, as described by Pan et al. Not opened.
numbers: Not extracted.
limits: Known only through citation in Pan et al.
agent_relevance: Source of the empowerment values used for the LLM comparison.
